name: Maang
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: only Hsiu 2014 wordlist attested; no description located

sources.citation: Wikipedia (zh) 末昂语 and (en) Maang language, raw wikitext, accessed 2026-09-17
sources.note: Secondary; phonology paragraph (from Zhou 2014) lists initials/finals/tones only; no stress. Reference lists used to identify Wu 1993, Zhou 2014, Wang 2018, Lama 2012, Hsiu 2014/2017.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Mondzish: a new subgroup of Lolo-Burmese. Proceedings of the 14th International Symposium on Chinese Languages and Linguistics (IsCLL-14). Taipei: Academia Sinica. 20 pp.
sources.note: Comparative subgrouping paper; Maang data taken from Lama (2012), Longyang village; forms carry tone numbers; the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the text (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing). Notes that Wu Zili (1993) was the first documentation of Mo'ang.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page maan1239 and sources.bib entries 688722, 688454, 669958
sources.note: Only three refs (Zhou 2014, Wu 1993, Moseley 2010); no descriptive ref with listed by Glottolog as a grammar/phonology.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2017. Meang audio word list. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.1123373
sources.note: 175 wav files + wordlist from Dala village, Napo County (Meang variety); no stress information.

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) Languages: A Study from the Perspectives of Shared Innovation and Phylogenetic Estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. 399 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: pp. 84-85 (pdf 103-104): 'Maang has 36 initials, 63 vowels (20 monophthongs, 20 diphthongs, 2 triphthongs, 17 finals with nasal codas, and 4 finals with stop codas), and 5 tones (/55/, /44/, /33/, /35/, and /21/) (LM Self-data 2003).' No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the dissertation (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.citation: Wu Zili 武自立. 1993. 云南富宁未昂话初探. 民族语文 1993(2). 11 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: First sketch with a 语音 section; 民族语文 sketches of this era sometimes note 重音 in disyllables. CNKI full text paywalled.

sources.citation: Wang Zhanling 王战领. 2023. 云南富宁末昂语研究. PhD dissertation, Shanghai Normal University, supervisor 王双成. 308 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Most recent and probably fullest description (308 pp.); a modern dissertation phonology chapter is likely to address stress/prominence explicitly. Copy at National Library of China (北区学位论文阅览室); probably also in the CNKI dissertation database (paywalled).

sources.note: The only published full description; the 中国新发现语言研究丛书 template has a 语音 chapter (声母/韵母/声调/音节) that is where a 重音/轻重音 statement would sit. Held by Library of Congress (LCCN 2013378352, PL3311.Y5 Z455 2014) and OCLC 883619789.

sources.note: CNKI-oversea abstract: uses word-rank theory to show Mo'ang is Yi-branch, discusses coda retention and deep contact with Zhuang; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wu Zili 武自立. 1993. 云南富宁未昂话初探 [A preliminary study of the Mo'ang language of Funing County, Yunnan]. 民族语文 1993(2). 11 pp.

sources.access_detail: digital copy exists; only the abstract or an excerpt is open
sources.note: CNKI abstract (via the Internet Archive): about 5,000 speakers in Longyang, Longmai, Mula, Ligong (Funing) and Zhezhang, Dana, Nianbi (Guangxi); '本文从语音、词汇、语法3个方面作简要介绍' (brief introduction to phonology, lexicon, grammar). Full text paywalled on CNKI; abstract says nothing about stress.
